safety_verdicts.content: Patient's wife and one child are also unwell with vomiting, but no diarrhea.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated mentions only the child vomiting (no diarrhea) but does not include that the wife was also unwell with vomiting.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting that the wife was also vomiting slightly reduces the accuracy of the infectious exposure history and may affect interpretation of likely viral household spread versus isolated foodborne illness and related counseling (e.g., infection control). Clinical management for uncomplicated gastroenteritis is unlikely to change materially based on this detail.

safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failure to document safety-net advice to seek earlier review if worsening can delay escalation for dehydration, persistent fever, blood in stool, or sepsis red flags. This can adversely affect outcomes by postponing needed reassessment, labs, or IV fluids.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Neither Gold nor transcript documents allergies status.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Stating or implying “no allergies” when allergy status was not assessed can mislead downstream clinicians and result in administration of an allergen (e.g., antibiotics/NSAIDs), with potential for severe reactions including anaphylaxis. Allergy documentation errors are high-risk because they can directly drive unsafe prescribing.
